doc33754: music of dominican republic merengue is musical genre native to dominican republic it has moderate to very fast 2 4 rhythm played on güira metal scraper and double headed tambora accordion is also common traditional accordion based merengue is usually termed merengue típico and is still played by living accordionists like francisco ulloa fefita la grande el ciego de nagua and rafaelito román more modern merengues incorporate electric instruments and influences from salsa and rock and roll choruses are often sung in call and response form by two or three back up singers or more traditionally by musicians playing tambora or güira beginning in 1960s dancing became part of singers work with johnny ventura s combo show format and is now staple of many of genre s biggest stars lyrically irony and double entendres are common merengue continued to be limited in popularity to lower classes especially in cibao area in early 20th century artists like juan f garcía juan espínola and julio alberto hernández tried to move merengue into mainstream but failed largely due to social prejudices some success occurred after nationalistic feelings arose among cibao elite who resented u s occupation of country from 1916 1924 legend has it that at this time faster merengue típico cibaeño was slowed down to accommodate american soldiers who couldn t dance difficult steps of merengue this mid tempo version was called pambiche major mainstream acceptance started with rafael trujillo s rise to power in early 1930s
doc33755: music of dominican republic dictator rafael trujillo who seized presidency of dominican republic in 1930 helped merengue to become national symbol of island up until his assassination in 1961 being that he was of humble origins he had been barred from elite social clubs he was therefore resentful of these elite sophisticates and began promoting cibao style merengue forcing all social classes to participate in low class dance at trujillo s command virtually all musical groups had to compose merengues praising trujillo s dictatorship its guidelines and actions of his party trujillo even made it mandatory for urban dance bands to include merengue in their repertoire also piano and brass instruments were added in merengue oriented big bands trend towards upward mobility popularizing by luis alberti s group in santiago de los caballeros on other hand merengue that continued to use accordion became known rather disrespectfully as perico ripiao ripped parrot it was because of all this that merengue became and still is dominican republicâ s national music and dance

doc46190: history of botany italian physician andrea caesalpino 1519 1603 studied medicine and taught botany at university of pisa for about 40 years eventually becoming director of botanic garden of pisa from 1554 to 1558 his sixteen volume de plantis 1583 described 1500 plants and his herbarium of 260 pages and 768 mounted specimens still remains caesalpino proposed classes based largely on detailed structure of flowers and fruit 59 he also applied concept of genus 67 he was first to try and derive principles of natural classification reflecting overall similarities between plants and he produced classification scheme well in advance of its day 68 gaspard bauhin 1560 1624 produced two influential publications prodromus theatrici botanici 1620 and pinax 1623 these brought order to 6000 species now described and in latter he used binomials and synonyms that may well have influenced linnaeus s thinking he also insisted that taxonomy should be based on natural affinities 69
doc46192: history of botany above all it was swedish carl linnaeus 1707 1778 who eased task of plant cataloguing he adopted sexual system of classification using stamens and pistils as important characters among his most important publications were systema naturae 1735 genera plantarum 1737 and philosophia botanica 1751 but it was in his species plantarum 1753 that he gave every species binomial thus setting path for future accepted method of designating names of all organisms linnaean thought and books dominated world of taxonomy for nearly century 73 his sexual system was later elaborated by bernard de jussieu 1699 1777 whose nephew antoine laurent de jussieu 1748 1836 extended it yet again to include about 100 orders present day families 74 frenchman michel adanson 1727 1806 in his familles des plantes 1763 1764 apart from extending current system of family names emphasized that natural classification must be based on consideration of all characters even though these may later be given different emphasis according to their diagnostic value for particular plant group adanson s method has in essence been followed to this day 75

doc77007: c4 carbon fixation c4 fixation is elaboration of more common c3 carbon fixation and is believed to have evolved more recently c4 overcomes tendency of enzyme rubisco to wastefully fix oxygen rather than carbon dioxide in process of photorespiration this is achieved by ensuring that rubisco works in environment where there is lot of carbon dioxide and very little oxygen co2 is shuttled via malate or aspartate from mesophyll cells to bundle sheath cells in these bundle sheath cells co2 is released by decarboxylation of malate c4 plants use pep carboxylase to capture more co2 in mesophyll cells pep carboxylase 3 carbons binds to co2 to make oxaloacetic acid oaa oaa then makes malate 4 carbons malate enters bundle sheath cells and releases co2 these additional steps however require more energy in form of atp using this extra energy c4 plants are able to more efficiently fix carbon in drought high temperatures and limitations of nitrogen or co2 since more common c3 pathway does not require this extra energy it is more efficient in other conditions
doc77010: c4 carbon fixation in c3 plants first step in light independent reactions of photosynthesis involves fixation of co2 by enzyme rubisco into 3 phosphoglycerate however due to dual carboxylase and oxygenase activity of rubisco some part of substrate is oxidized rather than carboxylated resulting in loss of substrate and consumption of energy in what is known as photorespiration in order to bypass photorespiration pathway c4 plants have developed mechanism to efficiently deliver co2 to rubisco enzyme they utilize their specific leaf anatomy where chloroplasts exist not only in mesophyll cells in outer part of their leaves but in bundle sheath cells as well instead of direct fixation to rubisco in calvin cycle co2 is incorporated into 4 carbon organic acid which has ability to regenerate co2 in chloroplasts of bundle sheath cells bundle sheath cells can then utilize this co2 to generate carbohydrates by conventional c3 pathway
doc77011: c4 carbon fixation first step in pathway is conversion of pyruvate to phosphoenolpyruvate pep by enzyme pyruvate orthophosphate dikinase this reaction requires inorganic phosphate and atp plus pyruvate producing phosphoenolpyruvate amp and inorganic pyrophosphate ppi next step is fixation of co2 into oxaloacetate by enzyme pep carboxylase both of these steps occur in mesophyll cells

doc267320: action potential neurons are electrically excitable cells composed in general of one or more dendrites single soma single axon and one or more axon terminals dendrites are cellular projections whose primary function is to receive synaptic signals their protrusions known as dendritic spines are designed to capture neurotransmitters released by presynaptic neuron they have high concentration of ligand gated ion channels these spines have thin neck connecting bulbous protrusion to dendrite this ensures that changes occurring inside spine are less likely to affect neighboring spines dendritic spine can with rare exception see ltp act as independent unit dendrites extend from soma which houses nucleus and many of normal eukaryotic organelles unlike spines surface of soma is populated by voltage activated ion channels these channels help transmit signals generated by dendrites emerging out from soma is axon hillock this region is characterized by having very high concentration of voltage activated sodium channels in general it is considered to be spike initiation zone for action potentials 13 multiple signals generated at spines and transmitted by soma all converge here immediately after axon hillock is axon this is thin tubular protrusion traveling away from soma axon is insulated by myelin sheath myelin is composed of either schwann cells in peripheral nervous system or oligodendrocytes in central nervous system both of which are types of glial cells although glial cells are not involved with transmission of electrical signals they communicate and provide important biochemical support to neurons 14 to be specific myelin wraps multiple times around axonal segment forming thick fatty layer that prevents ions from entering or escaping axon this insulation prevents significant signal decay as well as ensuring faster signal speed this insulation however has restriction that no channels can be present on surface of axon there are therefore regularly spaced patches of membrane which have no insulation these nodes of ranvier can be considered to be mini axon hillocks as their purpose is to boost signal in order to prevent significant signal decay at furthest end axon loses its insulation and begins to branch into several axon terminals these presynaptic terminals or synaptic boutons are specialized area within axon of presynaptic cell that contains neurotransmitters enclosed in small membrane bound spheres called synaptic vesicles

doc461869: polar easterlies polar easterlies also polar hadley cells are dry cold prevailing winds that blow from high pressure areas of polar highs at north and south poles towards low pressure areas within westerlies at high latitudes 1 cold air subsides at poles creating high pressure forcing equatorward outflow of air that outflow is then deflected westward by coriolis effect unlike westerlies in middle latitudes polar easterlies are often weak and irregular these prevailing winds blow from polar easterlies are one of five primary wind zones known as wind belts that make up our atmosphere s circulatory system this particular belt of wind begins at approximately 60 degrees north and south latitude and reaches to poles when air moves near poles cold temperatures shrink air this promotes air from warmer latitudes to flow into area causing polar high pressure zone air from this high pressure zone then rushes toward low pressure zone surrounding sub polar region flow of air is altered by earth s rotation and deflected west hence name between high and low pressure zones temperature and air pressure differentials and earth s rotation combine to form global currents

doc466964: interstitial fluid lymphatic system is collection system which starts in same tissue space as initial lymph collectors that have fenestrated openings to allow fluid and particles to enter these initial lymph collectors are valveless vessels and go on to form precollector vessels which have rudimentary valves which are not considered to be fully functional these structures then form increasingly larger lymphatic vessels which form co laterals in animals lower than mammals these vessels have lymph hearts which possess stretch receptors and smooth muscle tissue embedded in their walls lymphatic vessels make their way to lymph nodes and from lymph nodes vessels form into trunks which connect to internal jugular group of veins in neck lymphatic system once thought to be passive is now known to be active pumping system with segments exhibiting function similar to that of peristalsis

doc543513: history of psychology whereas würzburgers debated with wundt mainly on matters of method another german movement centered in berlin took issue with widespread assumption that aim of psychology should be to break consciousness down into putative basic elements instead they argued that psychological whole has priority and that parts are defined by structure of whole rather than vice versa thus school was named gestalt german term meaning approximately form or configuration it was led by max wertheimer 1880 1943 wolfgang köhler 1887 1967 and kurt koffka 1886 1941 wertheimer had been student of austrian philosopher christian von ehrenfels 1859 1932 who claimed that in addition to sensory elements of perceived object there is extra element which though in some sense derived from organization of standard sensory elements is also to be regarded as being element in its own right he called this extra element gestalt qualität or form quality for instance when one hears melody one hears notes plus something in addition to them which binds them together into tune gestalt qualität it is presence of this gestalt qualität which according to von ehrenfels allows tune to be transposed to new key using completely different notes but still retain its identity wertheimer took more radical line that what is given me by melody does not arise as secondary process from sum of pieces as such instead what takes place in each single part already depends upon what whole is 1925 1938 in other words one hears melody first and only then may perceptually divide it up into notes similarly in vision one sees form of circle first it is given im mediately i e its apprehension is not mediated by process of part summation only after this primary apprehension might one notice that it is made up of lines or dots or stars

doc637022: group 12 element although group 12 lies in d block of modern 18 column periodic table d electrons of zinc cadmium and almost always mercury behave as core electrons and do not take part in bonding this behavior is similar to that of main group elements but is in stark contrast to that of neighboring group 11 elements copper silver and gold which also have filled d subshells in their ground state electron configuration but behave chemically as transition metals for example bonding in chromium ii sulfide crs involves mainly 3d electrons that in iron ii sulfide fes involves both 3d and 4s electrons but that of zinc sulfide zns involves only 4s electrons and 3d electrons behave as core electrons indeed useful comparison can be made between their properties and first two members of group 2 beryllium and magnesium and in earlier short form periodic table layouts this relationship is illustrated more clearly for instance zinc and cadmium are similar to beryllium and magnesium in their atomic radii ionic radii electronegativities and also in structure of their binary compounds and their ability to form complex ions with many nitrogen and oxygen ligands such as complex hydrides and amines however beryllium and magnesium are small atoms unlike heavier alkaline earth metals and like group 12 elements which have greater nuclear charge but same number of valence electrons and periodic trends down group 2 from beryllium to radium similar to that of alkali metals are not as smooth when going down from beryllium to mercury which is more similar to that of p block main groups due to d block and lanthanide contractions it is also d block and lanthanide contractions that give mercury many of its distinctive properties 28

doc759778: monsoon of south asia also known as thermal theory or differential heating of sea and land theory traditional theory portrays monsoon as large scale sea breeze it states that during hot subtropical summers massive landmass of indian peninsula heats up at different rate than surrounding seas resulting in pressure gradient from south to north this causes flow of moisture laden winds from sea to land on reaching land these winds rise because of geographical relief cooling adiabatically and leading to orographic rains this is southwest monsoon reverse happens during winter when land is colder than sea establishing pressure gradient from land to sea this causes winds to blow over indian subcontinent toward indian ocean in northeasterly direction causing northeast monsoon because southwest monsoon flows from sea to land it carries more moisture and therefore causes more rain than northeast monsoon only part of northeast monsoon passing over bay of bengal picks up moisture causing rain in andhra pradesh and tamil nadu during winter months

doc833620: plate tectonics outer layers of earth are divided into lithosphere and asthenosphere division is based on differences in mechanical properties and in method for transfer of heat lithosphere is cooler and more rigid while asthenosphere is hotter and flows more easily in terms of heat transfer lithosphere loses heat by conduction whereas asthenosphere also transfers heat by convection and has nearly adiabatic temperature gradient this division should not be confused with chemical subdivision of these same layers into mantle comprising both asthenosphere and mantle portion of lithosphere and crust given piece of mantle may be part of lithosphere or asthenosphere at different times depending on its temperature and pressure

doc836633: harpsichord first music written specifically for solo harpsichord was published around early 16th century composers who wrote solo harpsichord music were numerous during whole baroque era in european countries including italy germany england and france solo harpsichord compositions included dance suites fantasias and fugues among most famous composers who wrote for harpsichord were members of english virginal school of late renaissance notably william byrd ca 1540 1623 in france great number of highly characteristic solo works were created and compiled into four books of ordres by françois couperin 1668 1733 domenico scarlatti 1685 1757 began his career in italy but wrote most of his solo harpsichord works in spain his most famous work is his series of 555 harpsichord sonatas perhaps most celebrated composer who wrote for harpsichord was j s bach 1685 1750 whose solo works for instance well tempered clavier and goldberg variations continue to be performed very widely often on piano bach was also pioneer of harpsichord concerto both in works designated as such and in harpsichord part of his fifth brandenburg concerto

doc1204224: cerebellum purkinje cells are among most distinctive neurons in brain and one of earliest types to be recognized they were first described by czech anatomist jan evangelista purkyně in 1837 they are distinguished by shape of their dendritic tree dendrites branch very profusely but are severely flattened in plane perpendicular to cerebellar folds thus dendrites of purkinje cell form dense planar net through which parallel fibers pass at right angles 8 dendrites are covered with dendritic spines each of which receives synaptic input from parallel fiber purkinje cells receive more synaptic inputs than any other type of cell in brain estimates of number of spines on single human purkinje cell run as high as 200 000 8 large spherical cell bodies of purkinje cells are packed into narrow layer one cell thick of cerebellar cortex called purkinje layer after emitting collaterals that affect nearby parts of cortex their axons travel into deep cerebellar nuclei where they make on order of 1 000 contacts each with several types of nuclear cells all within small domain purkinje cells use gaba as their neurotransmitter and therefore exert inhibitory effects on their targets 8

doc1350992: neuron typical neuron consists of cell body soma dendrites and axon term neurite is used to describe either dendrite or axon particularly in its undifferentiated stage dendrites are thin structures that arise from cell body often extending for hundreds of micrometers and branching multiple times giving rise to complex dendritic tree axon also called nerve fiber is special cellular extension process that arises from cell body at site called axon hillock and travels for distance as far as 1 meter in humans or even more in other species most neurons receive signals via dendrites and send out signals down axon numerous axons are often bundled into fascicles that make up nerves in peripheral nervous system like strands of wire make up cables bundles of axons in central nervous system are called tracts cell body of neuron frequently gives rise to multiple dendrites but never to more than one axon although axon may branch hundreds of times before it terminates at majority of synapses signals are sent from axon of one neuron to dendrite of another there are however many exceptions to these rules for example neurons can lack dendrites or have no axon and synapses can connect axon to another axon or dendrite to another dendrite
doc1350996: neuron typical neuron is divided into three parts soma or cell body dendrites and axon soma is usually compact axon and dendrites are filaments that extrude from it dendrites typically branch profusely getting thinner with each branching and extending their farthest branches few hundred micrometers from soma axon leaves soma at swelling called axon hillock and can extend for great distances giving rise to hundreds of branches unlike dendrites axon usually maintains same diameter as it extends soma may give rise to numerous dendrites but never to more than one axon synaptic signals from other neurons are received by soma and dendrites signals to other neurons are transmitted by axon typical synapse then is contact between axon of one neuron and dendrite or soma of another synaptic signals may be excitatory or inhibitory if net excitation received by neuron over short period of time is large enough neuron generates brief pulse called action potential which originates at soma and propagates rapidly along axon activating synapses onto other neurons as it goes

doc1557542: arnold schoenberg later schoenberg was to develop most influential version of dodecaphonic also known as twelve tone method of composition which in french and english was given alternative name serialism by rené leibowitz and humphrey searle in 1947 this technique was taken up by many of his students who constituted so called second viennese school they included anton webern alban berg and hanns eisler all of whom were profoundly influenced by schoenberg he published number of books ranging from his famous harmonielehre theory of harmony to fundamentals of musical composition schoenberg 1967 many of which are still in print and used by musicians and developing composers
doc1557557: arnold schoenberg schoenberg s significant compositions in repertory of modern art music extend over period of more than 50 years traditionally they are divided into three periods though this division is arguably arbitrary as music in each of these periods is considerably varied idea that his twelve tone period represents stylistically unified body of works is simply not supported by musical evidence haimo 1990 4 and important musical characteristics especially those related to motivic development transcend these boundaries completely first of these periods 1894 1907 is identified in legacy of high romantic composers of late nineteenth century as well as with expressionist movements in poetry and art second 1908 1922 is typified by abandonment of key centers move often described though not by schoenberg as free atonality third from 1923 onward commences with schoenberg s invention of dodecaphonic or twelve tone compositional method schoenberg s best known students hanns eisler alban berg and anton webern followed schoenberg faithfully through each of these intellectual and aesthetic transitions though not without considerable experimentation and variety of approach

doc2214828: ultraviolet in general ultraviolet detectors use either solid state device such as one based on silicon carbide or aluminium nitride or gas filled tube as sensing element uv detectors that are sensitive to uv in any part of spectrum respond to irradiation by sunlight and artificial light burning hydrogen flame for instance radiates strongly in 185 to 260 nanometer range and only very weakly in ir region whereas coal fire emits very weakly in uv band yet very strongly at ir wavelengths thus fire detector that operates using both uv and ir detectors is more reliable than one with uv detector alone virtually all fires emit some radiation in uvc band whereas sun s radiation at this band is absorbed by earth s atmosphere result is that uv detector is solar blind meaning it will not cause alarm in response to radiation from sun so it can easily be used both indoors and outdoors

doc2253873: moseley s law moseley s law is empirical law concerning characteristic x rays that are emitted by atoms law was discovered and published by english physicist henry moseley in 1913 it is historically important in quantitatively justifying conception of nuclear model of atom with all or nearly all positive charges of atom located in nucleus and associated on integer basis with atomic number until moseley s work atomic number was merely element s place in periodic table and was not known to be associated with any measureable physical quantity 1 moseley was able to show that frequencies of certain characteristic x rays emitted from chemical elements are proportional to square of number which was close to element s atomic number finding which supported van den broek and bohr s model of atom in which atomic number is same as number of positive charges in nucleus of atom in brief law states that square root of frequency of emitted x ray is proportional to atomic number

doc2319513: brackish water this type of ecological succession from freshwater to marine ecosystem is typical of river estuaries river estuaries form important staging points during migration of anadromous and catadromous fish species such as salmon shad and eels giving them time to form social groups and to adjust to changes in salinity salmon are anadromous meaning they live in sea but ascend rivers to spawn eels are catadromous living in rivers and streams but returning to sea to breed besides species that migrate through estuaries there are many other fish that use them as nursery grounds for spawning or as places young fish can feed and grow before moving elsewhere herring and plaice are two commercially important species that use thames estuary for this purpose

doc2363844: agricultural soil science agricultural soil scientists study ways to make soils more productive they classify soils and test them to determine whether they contain nutrients vital to plant growth such nutritional substances include compounds of nitrogen phosphorus and potassium if certain soil is deficient in these substances fertilizers may provide them agricultural soil scientists investigate movement of nutrients through soil and amount of nutrients absorbed by plant s roots agricultural soil scientists also examine development of roots and their relation to soil some agricultural soil scientists try to understand structure and function of soils in relation to soil fertility they grasp structure of soil as porous solid solid frames of soil consist of mineral derived from rocks and organic matter originated from dead bodies of various organisms pore space of soil is essential for soil to become productive small pores serve as water reservoir supplying water to plants and other organisms in soil during rain less period water in small pores of soils is not pure water they call it soil solution in soil solution various plant nutrients derived from minerals and organic matters in soil are there this is measured through cation exchange capacity large pores serve as water drainage pipe to allow excessive water pass through soil during heavy rains they also serve as air tank to supply oxygen to plant roots and other living beings in soil in short agricultural soil scientists see soil as vessel most precious one for us containing all of substances needed by plants and other living beings on earth

doc2492559: berg wind although berg winds are often called föhn winds this is probably misnomer as föhn winds are rain shadow winds that result from air moving over mountain range resulting in precipitation on windward side this releases latent heat into atmosphere which is then warmed still further as air descends on leeward side e g chinook or original föhn 2 3 berg winds do not originate in precipitation but in mostly dry often arid central plateau of southern africa on other hand katabatic winds are technically drainage winds that carry high density usually cold air from high elevation down slope under force of gravity 3 these are thus fall winds which occur most typically down coastal ice slopes of antarctica and greenland berg winds blow off african escarpment in response to large scale weather systems in south atlantic ocean african interior and southern indian ocean
doc2492560: berg wind berg winds are usually accompanied by coastal lows 3 these coastal lows owe their existence to configuration of plateau escarpment and coastal plain see diagram on right above in that they are confined to coastal areas always below escarpment though they can arise almost anywhere along coast they often first appear on west coast or even on namibian coast they are then always propagated counter clockwise along south africa s coastline at between 30 60 km h from west coast southwards to cape peninsula and then eastward along south coast and finally north eastward along kwazulunatal coastline to finally dissipate north of durban due to divergence of coastline from plateau which disappears altogether in vicinity of limpopo valley 4 there is always hot off shore berg wind ahead of coastal low which can blow for several days or for only for few hours this is then followed by cool onshore winds which bring low cloud fog or drizzle to region but may on occasions produce substantial precipitation when coupled to approaching cold front 3
doc2492563: berg wind along south coast passage of coastal low is typically preceded by north easterly wind driven by south indian ocean anticyclone wind then backs quickly through northerly to north westerly as its temperature rises this is berg wind phase of coastal low wind then changes abruptly to strong cold south or south westerly wind called buster if change in wind speed is greater than 35 km h buster coincides with passage of pressure minimum onshore wind gradually diminishes in intensity during course of about day and is associated with cloudy misty or drizzly weather 3 4

doc2497702: nonpoint source pollution phosphorus is nutrient that occurs in many forms that are bioavailable it is notoriously over abundant in human sewage sludge it is main ingredient in many fertilizers used for agriculture as well as on residential and commercial properties and may become limiting nutrient in freshwater systems and some estuaries phosphorus is most often transported to water bodies via soil erosion because many forms of phosphorus tend to be adsorbed on to soil particles excess amounts of phosphorus in aquatic systems particularly freshwater lakes reservoirs and ponds leads to proliferation of microscopic algae called phytoplankton increase of organic matter supply due to excessive growth of phytoplankton is called eutrophication common symptom of eutrophication is algae blooms that can produce unsightly surface scums shade out beneficial types of plants produce taste and odor causing compounds and poison water due to toxins produced by algae these toxins are particular problem in systems used for drinking water because some toxins can cause human illness and removal of toxins is difficult and expensive bacterial decomposition of algal blooms consumes dissolved oxygen in water generating hypoxia with detrimental consequences for fish and aquatic invertebrates
